Change 2556 review status: LLM-Review +1 (PASS, 1 advisory), but Verified -1 — AND THE CI FAILURE IS NOT THIS CHANGE'S.

The failing test is `tests/unit/test_bug_claim_rca_sequence_docs.py::test_claim_time_exemption_type_registry_includes_bug`, which touches none of this change's three files. It asserts a literal SOURCE STRING, `_PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES = ("bug"`, appears in src/rebar/_commands/gates.py.

I verified this is a MAIN breakage, not something 2556 introduced: checked out pristine origin/main into the worktree and ran the test there — 1 failed, 5 passed, identical assertion. It also fails identically on py3.11, py3.12 and py3.13, so it is deterministic, not flaky, and no recheck is warranted.

Root cause is a semantic merge conflict between two changes that were each green alone, which per-patchset CI structurally cannot catch: change 2544 added the source-text assertion, while change 2530 (mirror F3) consolidated that constant into rebar.types, so gates.py now imports it and the asserted literal no longer exists. No textual conflict, so Gerrit's Rebase-If-Necessary had nothing to flag.

Already owned and being fixed elsewhere: bug `5550-603c` (seaisland-deformed-shrike), in_progress and claimed by another session, with a fix pushed as Gerrit change 2557. I am NOT duplicating that work. 2556 will be rebased and re-triggered once 2557 lands.

The one advisory on 2556 is non-blocking: NextBatchOut's newly-added _omit_when_unset behaviour is untested. Worth addressing on the next patch set, since the equivalent behaviour for the other models IS covered.
